name: Scholastic Corporation
domainRelevance: Scholastic is the largest publisher and distributor of children's educational materials in North America, commanding ~50% of the school book club market and operating in 180+ countries. Its portfolio spans trade publishing (Harry Potter, Clifford, The Baby-Sitters Club), educational content, and classroom book fairs—making it a primary vector for literacy formation and values transmission in K–12 education. The company's book-selection curation and distribution network directly shape reading habits and cultural narratives for 100+ million students annually.
portalRelevance: Scholastic serves as a critical financial-intelligence node for education-sector health, consumer discretionary spending on children's goods, and publishing-industry structural change. Its book-fair revenue, school-channel penetration, and trade-publishing performance signal household spending confidence, parental investment in education, and the viability of print-based content distribution in a digital-native generation. As a mid-cap equity with cyclical exposure to school budgets and consumer discretionary, Scholastic's earnings and cash-flow trajectory offer leading indicators for education spending and family-formation trends.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly school book-fair revenue and unit sales (disclosed in 10-Q; leading indicator of K–12 discretionary spending)
Trade publishing backlist performance and new-release sell-through rates (tracked via BookScan and internal sales reports)
International segment revenue from UK, Australia, and emerging markets (8-K events on acquisition/divestiture; 10-K Item 1A geographic breakdown)
Paper and freight cost inflation signals from supplier announcements and commodity indices (FRED CPIRECSL, freight indices)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification based on revenue growth trajectory, operating-margin trend, and free-cash-flow sign (quarterly 10-Q filings)
School-channel market-share position vs. competitors (Penguin Random House, Hachette, Simon & Schuster) via industry reports
Debt-to-EBITDA ratio and liquidity runway given seasonal working-capital swings (10-K Item 7 MD&A)
Digital-content adoption rate and e-book penetration as offset to print decline (investor calls, 10-K forward-looking statements)

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Print-to-digital transition risk: structural headwind vs. cyclical dip (pattern-match against Penguin Random House, HachettteBook Group margin compression 2020–2023)
School-budget cycle dependency: revenue cliff if K–12 discretionary spending contracts (correlation with state education appropriations, FRED CES7071100001)
Working-capital volatility: book-fair seasonality creates Q4 cash surge, Q1–Q2 burn (10-K Item 1A liquidity risk)
Acquisition integration risk: Scholastic has divested underperforming segments; assess synergy realization from retained assets (8-K M&A filings, 10-K Item 8 goodwill impairment)

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Investment thesis: cyclical recovery play if school budgets stabilize post-pandemic; long-duration print-to-digital transition requires margin discipline
Risk hedge: short paper/cardboard futures if commodity inflation persists; monitor freight indices for margin compression signals

Regulatory watch: FTC antitrust scrutiny on trade-publishing consolidation (Penguin Random House / Simon & Schuster merger review precedent); SEC disclosure of related-party transactions with book-club partners
Capital allocation: monitor dividend sustainability if free-cash-flow turns negative; assess share-buyback authorization vs. debt reduction priority

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Quarterly earnings-call monitoring for school-channel guidance revisions and international segment commentary
Book-fair revenue tracking as leading indicator; set alert thresholds for YoY decline >10%
Debt refinancing calendar: monitor maturity schedule and covenant compliance (10-K Item 5 debt table)
Competitive positioning: track market-share gains/losses vs. Amazon (direct-to-consumer children's books) and indie publishers via BookScan data

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Post-earnings validation: compare guidance vs. actuals for school-channel revenue and trade-publishing sell-through
Price reaction to 10-K filing: assess market's confidence in digital-transition narrative and margin-recovery path
Competitor earnings cross-check: Penguin Random House (private; monitor via news), Simon & Schuster (Paramount ownership; track via 10-K references)
Commodity-cost pass-through: measure gross-margin resilience vs. paper/freight inflation (10-Q Item 2 MD&A)

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Recalibrate school-budget sensitivity: if state education appropriations show structural decline, lower revenue-growth assumptions
Update digital-adoption curve: track e-book and audiobook revenue as % of total; adjust long-term margin expectations
Reassess working-capital model: if book-fair seasonality shifts (e.g., earlier/later timing), update cash-flow forecasts
Refine competitive-threat scoring: if Amazon or indie publishers gain school-channel share, increase competitive-risk weighting in phase classification

suppliers.name: International Paper Company

Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A as key supplier concentration risk.
